description: False-colour satellite map showing the Santa Pola salines, Spain, captured on 2011-08-12 by Spot 5 (2.5 m resolution, 1/2/3 band combination). The map depicts a coastal environment with deep blue open water, extensive lighter blue/grey/brown intertidal flats featuring intricate channels, and landmasses. Vegetated areas on land appear bright red, indicating the use of a false-colour infrared band combination common in satellite imagery. A prominent green polygon boundary delineates a large coastal zone encompassing both terrestrial and intertidal features, likely corresponding to a Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) CORINE Land Cover (CLC) mapping unit, specifically CLC class 423 "Intertidal flats". The image visualises the definition of intertidal flats as generally vegetationless expanses of mud, sand, or rock between high and low water marks. The data source is CNES 2011©, distributed by Airbus DS/Spot Image.
